questions.q: Knights Valley AVA, one of the Court's Certified names, lies in which county?
questions.exp: Knights Valley is a Sonoma County AVA of 1983, though it runs up to the county line just north-west of Calistoga, which is why it is so often misplaced. It is the warmest corner of Sonoma, planted to Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay on volcanic and alluvial soils; the Court's other Certified names, Mount Veeder, Calistoga and Yountville, all lie in Napa County.

questions.q: Which river runs down the valley floor between the Mayacamas and the Vaca ranges and empties south into San Pablo Bay?
questions.exp: The Napa River rises near Mount St Helena and flows south the length of the valley to San Pablo Bay, the water that sends cool air and fog north into Carneros each afternoon. The Court lists it among the North Coast's physical features with the Sonoma, Mayacamas and Vaca ranges, the bay itself and the Petaluma Wind Gap.

questions.q: What does the Court say mountain vineyards in the North Coast give compared with the valley floors?
opts: Lower yields and bigger diurnal shifts
Higher yields and smaller diurnal shifts
Higher yields and bigger diurnal shifts
Lower yields and smaller diurnal shifts
questions.exp: The Court's cell pairs the two: mountain sites crop lighter on thin, rocky soils and, by its account, swing further between day and night, so Howell Mountain, Mount Veeder or Spring Mountain Cabernet comes in small berried, deeply coloured and firmly tannic. The same cell adds that northern Napa, towards Calistoga, is warmer than the bay end.

questions.q: By which method does the Court say North Coast sparkling wine is most commonly made?
questions.exp: Carneros and the Anderson Valley give the high acid base wine, and houses such as Schramsberg, Domaine Carneros, Roederer Estate and Iron Horse make it the Champagne way, with the second fermentation in the bottle the guest is poured from and long ageing on the lees. Tank method wine is refermented in a pressurised vat instead, the Prosecco route.

questions.q: Which red grape is the Anderson Valley in Mendocino County best known for?
questions.exp: The Anderson Valley opens to the Pacific at its western end, and its fog and cool nights suit Pinot Noir, for still wine and as sparkling base beside Chardonnay; Roederer Estate has farmed there since 1982. The Court asks the grapes matched to the AVAs: Cabernet to the warm Napa benches and Alexander Valley, Zinfandel to Dry Creek Valley.

questions.q: What share of the grapes in an Estate Bottled wine must come from vineyards the winery owns or controls?
questions.exp: Estate Bottled is the strictest American label term: every grape from the winery's own or controlled vineyards, crushed, fermented, finished and bottled on its premises in one continuous process. The Court's cell says the vineyards must lie in the same county; the federal rule draws the line at the AVA named on the label, in which the winery must also stand.

questions.q: A North Coast label names a grape, an AVA, a vintage and a single vineyard. Which of the four claims asks the smallest share of the wine's fruit?
questions.exp: The grape variety needs only 75 per cent of the wine, the AVA 85 per cent, and the vintage and the single vineyard 95 per cent each, the ladder the Court prints for the North Coast; Estate Bottled, at the top, asks 100 per cent from the winery's own vineyards. So a Cabernet Sauvignon may hold up to a quarter of Merlot and still carry the one grape's name.

questions.q: A guest asks what the word Reserve guarantees on a Sonoma Cabernet. What does American law say it guarantees?
questions.exp: Reserve has no legal meaning in the United States, so it may mark a winery's best barrels or nothing more than a higher price; Old Vine, Barrel Select and Private Reserve are just as unregulated. Spain's Reserva and Italy's Riserva are the opposite case, with ageing minimums written into law.

questions.q: Founded at St Helena in 1876 and kept open through Prohibition, which house completes the Court's Introductory trio of producers beside Opus One and Robert Mondavi?
questions.exp: Beringer was founded by the German brothers Jacob and Frederick Beringer and is reckoned the Napa Valley's oldest continuously operating winery, having kept working through Prohibition by making sacramental wine. Its Private Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay are the wines a list carries.

questions.q: Silver Oak Cellars, a Court producer at the Certified level, matures its Cabernet Sauvignon in which oak alone?
questions.exp: Silver Oak, founded in 1972, ages its Napa Valley and Alexander Valley Cabernets only in American oak, which ties it to the Court's Style row: American oak gives more overt vanilla, coconut and dill, French oak subtler spice and finer tannin. Most Napa Cabernet is raised largely in new French barrels, which makes Silver Oak the exception to know.

questions.q: Which Hungarian émigré founded the Buena Vista winery at Sonoma in 1857 and brought European vine cuttings to California?
questions.exp: Agoston Haraszthy, who styled himself a count, founded Buena Vista in 1857, often called California's first premium winery, and after a European tour in 1861 imported cuttings of hundreds of varieties for the state. The Court pairs him at the Introductory level with Robert Mondavi, André Tchelistcheff and the Paris tasting of 1976.

questions.q: Charles Krug, a Certified name in the Court's history row, founded his St Helena winery in which year?
questions.exp: Charles Krug opened his St Helena winery in 1861, reckoned the oldest winery still working in the Napa Valley, and the Mondavi family bought it in 1943 before the split that produced the Oakville winery of 1966. The other years belong to Buena Vista in Sonoma (1857), Beringer (1876) and Inglenook (1879); the Court's other Certified figure, Warren Winiarski, founded Stag's Leap Wine Cellars, whose 1973 Cabernet won the red flight in Paris.
